scene: A fisherman and a market vendor stand talking in a flat rice paddy, both alive and unhurried, the horizon dead level behind them.
teaches: A live syllable is a mid tone for low and mid class alike — the two agree here, which is why they share the scene.
prompt: A fisherman in a conical straw hat and rolled-up trousers and a market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron standing and talking in a flooded green rice paddy, both upright, unhurt and relaxed, the horizon a dead flat line behind them under a wide open sky.

scene: A monk walks down into a dip and then climbs a long hill path, alive and steady, robes bright against the slope.
teaches: High class is the one exception on a live syllable: it rises where the others stay level.
prompt: A monk in an orange robe with a shaved head walking up a long steep hill path, seen from below, the path dipping in the foreground and then rising sharply to a high ridge against the sky.

scene: A fisherman on a rooftop is killed instantly by a single lightning strike — one flash, already over.
teaches: Low class, dead syllable, short vowel: high tone. Length only ever matters here.
prompt: A fisherman in a conical straw hat and rolled-up trousers standing on the flat roof of a building, at the instant a jagged white lightning bolt hits him. His body arches backwards, arms flung wide, a blinding flash at the point of impact.

scene: The same fisherman goes over a waterfall and drowns slowly in the pool below, the fall drawn out and unhurried.
teaches: Low class, dead syllable, long vowel: falling. The slow death is the long vowel.
prompt: A fisherman in a conical straw hat and rolled-up trousers sinking slowly beneath the surface of a deep green pool at the foot of a tall waterfall, arms drifting upward above him, a long trail of bubbles rising to the light.

scene: A market vendor and a monk both fall down the same well and do not come back up.
teaches: Dead syllable, mid or high class: low tone, and the vowel's length changes nothing. Four rules, one well.
prompt: A market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron and a monk in an orange robe with a shaved head falling head-first down a round stone well shaft, arms and legs flailing above them, seen from inside the well looking up at the bright circular opening.

scene: A one-pointed spear stands driven into the well's rim, and the market vendor and the monk are already gone down the shaft.
teaches: Mai ek over mid or high class: low tone. The one-pointed spear is the mark, and it decides the tone whatever the syllable was doing.
prompt: A plain one-pointed spear standing upright, driven into the stone rim of a round well. A market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron and a monk in an orange robe with a shaved head tumbling down the dark shaft beside it, arms above their heads, seen from the well mouth looking down.

scene: A two-pronged spear pitches the market vendor and the monk over the lip of the waterfall together.
teaches: Mai tho over mid or high class: falling. Two prongs, two.
prompt: A market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron and a monk in an orange robe with a shaved head falling head-first over the lip of a tall waterfall, upside down in the white water. A large two-pronged spear is planted at the clifftop above them, both prongs clearly visible against the sky.

scene: The same one-pointed spear sends the fisherman over the waterfall instead of into the well.
teaches: Mai ek over low class: falling, not low. The same spear, a different end — low class takes the marks its own way.
prompt: A fisherman in a conical straw hat and rolled-up trousers falling head-first over the lip of a tall waterfall. A plain one-pointed spear is planted at the clifftop above him, its single point sharp against the sky.

scene: A two-pronged spear lifts the fisherman up onto the rooftop and leaves him there.
teaches: Mai tho over low class: high. Hauled up where the other two were dragged down.
prompt: A fisherman in a conical straw hat and rolled-up trousers lying sprawled on a flat rooftop against the sky, a large two-pronged spear planted upright on the roof beside him, both prongs clearly visible.

scene: The market vendor stands alone on the rooftop holding a trident, its three points against the sky.
teaches: Mai tri only ever sits on mid class, and gives high. Three prongs, and tri is three.
prompt: A market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron standing alone on a flat rooftop, holding a large three-pronged trident upright in both hands, its three points sharp and clear against an open sky. Nobody else on the roof.

scene: The market vendor carries a four-tined pitchfork up the hill path, climbing alone.
teaches: Mai chattawa only ever sits on mid class, and gives rising. Four tines, and chattawa is four.
prompt: A market vendor in a flat straw hat and a work apron climbing alone up a steep hill path, holding up a single four-tined wooden pitchfork, exactly four straight tines spread wide and clear against the open sky.
